A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RiverMamba and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GloFAS and GRDC forecasting experiments, ablations, computational measurements, and flood case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds ablation results and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, serialization, LOAN, forecasting heads, weighted loss, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Added explanations of broadcasting and GRDC loss masking clarify implementation. Alternative activations and weighting are tested as ablations, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GloFAS, GRDC, meteorological inputs, and static-attribute datasets. HydroRIVERS experiments, ungauged-station evaluation, and the regional flood case studies already appear in v1. Added experiments stay within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds LSTM comparators to the computational-efficiency evaluation in Appendix G, Table 18; v1's efficiency comparisons concern Mamba and Flash-Attention. Accuracy-comparison methods remain unchanged. Clarifying which LSTM results come from the authors' implementation does not establish a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce loss-offset and activation controls, plus single-A100 timing across input-point counts and four-day versus one-year LSTM histories. Existing accuracy splits, station selection, and model budgets remain unchanged. GRDC timestamp alignment is newly documented, without evidence of a revised evaluation or rerun.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds lead-time-weighting-only and forecast-only-LOAN controls. New Appendices F.5–F.6 test an additive flood-weight offset and ReLU versus GELU, while Appendix G extends runtime analysis. These are targeted additions to an already extensive ablation suite.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations over three runs for the principal comparisons and describe three independently seeded LSTM models. Existing distribution plots are retained. The additions introduce no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: v3 reports additional ablation and timing results: for example, lead-time weighting alone gives KGE/F1 of 0.9136/0.2593, and Table 18 reports 4.739 seconds for RiverMamba at 1.5 million points. Main Tables 1 and 3 retain their results after conversion from percentage-style values to decimals; this is not improved accuracy.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 removes v1's blanket assertion that both Mamba and Flash-Attention have linear complexity and instead explicitly describes linear memory scaling. This is a limited correction to the complexity characterization. Equations 1–20 and the mathematical definitions otherwise remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace claims of a global receptive field and global channel-network routing with a very large spatiotemporal receptive field covering river networks. The central claims of global 0.05-degree forecasting, seven-day lead times, and superior benchmark performance remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications: return-period exceedance is a proxy for hydrological extremity rather than necessarily actual flooding, and operational deployment faces ERA5-Land's five-day availability delay versus the assumed one day. It also clarifies residual GloFAS dependence in the input-removal ablation and discusses LOAN's KGE/F1 tradeoff.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v3 documents a specific code and processing-script repository, a processed-data DOI, and access instructions while retaining GRDC licensing constraints. It also clarifies timestamp synchronization, GRDC loss masking, LSTM reimplementation, and ablation dependencies. This substantially expands documented reproducibility and resource access.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Floodsformer, DRUM, FloodGNN-GRU, and several spatially distributed or physics-informed routing studies, broadening the positioning against hydrological approaches that model routing. The main research positioning remains recognizable. Publication updates and consolidated duplicate references are not new related work.

P1.justification: v3 edits prose throughout, expands selected method and baseline explanations, adds experimental subheadings, and corrects the author's name from Zahng to Zhang. References are consolidated after the appendices, and case studies become a separate appendix. The overall narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 2, adds Tables 16–18, reformats score displays as decimals, and clarifies LSTM captions. Figure 4 receives cosmetic changes, Figure 11 moves, and the two Sauer River case-study figures exchange order. Most figures and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility, clarifies baseline provenance, and better qualifies operational applicability and the meaning of flood predictions. Added controls and timing measurements provide useful, limited evidence while the principal method and benchmark findings remain stable. The new loss-offset study's blanket negative conclusion overlooks mixed test results in Table 16, but this localized weakness does not outweigh the gains in transparency and interpretation.
